title: An isomorphism on completed stalks implies etaleness near the point
statement: Let $f:Z\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $T$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $z\in Z$, set $t=f(z)$, and write $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T,t}$ and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Z,z}$ for the completions of the local rings at their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose that the homomorphism $\widehat f_z^{\sharp}:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T,t}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Z,z}$ induced by the actual stalk map $f_z^{\sharp}$ is an isomorphism. Then there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq Z$ containing $z$ such that $f|_W:W\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and the map $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(z)$ induced by $f$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0CAV, lemma-isomorphism-approximation, proof, first paragraph: an isomorphism on completed stalks implies smoothness by Tag 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point), unramifiedness, and hence etaleness by Morphisms Tag 02GK (lemma-etale-smooth-unramified).

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ and $\varphi=f_z^\sharp:A\to B$. These are Noetherian local rings: choose a Noetherian affine neighbourhood of $t$ and a finite-type affine chart of $f$ containing $z$. Its source coordinate ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Both stalks are localizations of these affine coordinate rings by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. In particular their maximal ideals are finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $i_A:A\to\widehat A$, $i_B:B\to\widehat B$ and $h=\widehat\varphi$, so $h i_A=i_B\varphi$ and $h$ is the given isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, lemma-isomorphism-approximation, first proof paragraph: local Noetherian setup for the completed-stalk criterion

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], the maximal ideals of $\widehat A$ and $\widehat B$ are $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ and $\mathfrak m_B\widehat B$, and the canonical completion maps identify their residue fields with those of $A$ and $B$. A ring isomorphism preserves units and therefore carries the unique maximal ideal onto the unique maximal ideal, as well as its square onto its square. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] with $N=1,2$ on both sides. It follows that $\varphi$ induces isomorphisms $A/\mathfrak m_A^N\to B/\mathfrak m_B^N$ for $N=1,2$: these maps are the quotient maps induced by $h$, since $h i_A=i_B\varphi$. In particular the actual residue-field map $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism, proving the second conclusion already.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, first proof paragraph: residue and first-order information in the completed stalk map

proof.text: Let $J=\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. For $b\in\mathfrak m_B$, the isomorphism modulo squares of step 2 supplies $a\in A$ with $b-\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak m_B^2$. Its reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_B$ is zero, so the injectivity of the residue-field map implies $a\in\mathfrak m_A$. Thus $\mathfrak m_B=J+\mathfrak m_B^2$. The finite $B$-module $M=\mathfrak m_B/J$ satisfies $\mathfrak m_BM=M$. The Jacobson radical of a local ring is its unique maximal ideal, so [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] gives $M=0$, that is $J=\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, first proof paragraph: maximal-ideal equality behind the unramifiedness assertion

proof.text: To prove smoothness at $z$, apply the small-Artinian-extension criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point]. Fix one of its diagrams, with $q:C'\twoheadrightarrow C$ a small extension and $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}C\to Z$, $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}C'\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime] the spectra have one point; the point of $\alpha$ is $z$, and the point of $\beta$ is consequently $t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] these morphisms correspond to local homomorphisms $b:B\to C$ and $a:A\to C'$. Their compatibility is $qa=b\varphi$, by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition]. It remains to construct a local $c:B\to C'$ with $qc=b$ and $c\varphi=a$.

source.place: Tag 02HX, lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point, (3) implies (1), applied in Tag 0CAV

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] choose $r,s\ge1$ such that $\mathfrak m_{C'}^{r}=0$ and $\mathfrak m_C^s=0$. Locality gives $a(\mathfrak m_A^r)=0$ and $b(\mathfrak m_B^s)=0$. Factor $a$ through $\bar a:A/\mathfrak m_A^r\to C'$ and $b$ through $\bar b:B/\mathfrak m_B^s\to C$, and define $\widehat a=\bar a\pi_{A,r}:\widehat A\to C'$ and $\widehat b=\bar b\pi_{B,s}:\widehat B\to C$ using the projections of [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. Then $\widehat a i_A=a$, $\widehat b i_B=b$, and these maps kill $(\mathfrak m_A\widehat A)^r$ and $(\mathfrak m_B\widehat B)^s$ respectively. Here extension of an ideal commutes with powers: both ideals are generated by the same products of $r$, respectively $s$, elements of the original maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, first proof paragraph, lifting through the inverse completed map for the tests of Tag 02HX

proof.text: The homomorphisms $q\widehat a$ and $\widehat b h$ from $\widehat A$ to $C$ agree on $i_A(A)$ because $qa=b\varphi$ and $hi_A=i_B\varphi$. They both kill $(\mathfrak m_A\widehat A)^n$ for $n\ge r,s$, since $h$ carries the extended maximal ideal of $A$ onto that of $B$ (step 2). For any $u\in\widehat A$, choose $a_0\in A$ representing $\pi_{A,n}(u)\in A/\mathfrak m_A^n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], $u-i_A(a_0)$ belongs to that killed ideal. Consequently $q\widehat a(u)=qa(a_0)=b\varphi(a_0)=\widehat b h(u)$, proving $q\widehat a=\widehat b h$. Set $c=\widehat a h^{-1}i_B$. Then $qc=\widehat b i_B=b$ and $c\varphi=\widehat a h^{-1}i_B\varphi=\widehat a i_A=a$.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, first proof paragraph: explicit compatibility of the Artinian lift with both arrows

proof.text: The map $c$ is local. Indeed a surjective map of local rings $q:C'\to C$ has $q^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_{C'}$: the inverse image is maximal and $C'$ has only one maximal ideal. As $qc=b$ and $b$ is local, $c^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{C'})=\mathfrak m_B$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] constructs $\gamma:\operatorname{Spec}C'\to Z$ from $(z,c)$. The equalities $qc=b$ and $c\varphi=a$, together with [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition] and the injectivity in the same local-spectrum bijection, give $\gamma\circ\operatorname{Spec}q=\alpha$ and $f\gamma=\beta$. All diagrams in [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point] therefore lift. Its hypotheses hold by the assumptions on $T$ and $f$, so there is an open $U\subseteq Z$ containing $z$ with $f|_U$ smooth.

source.place: Tags 02HX and 0CAV: finish the smoothness argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-unramified-maximal-ideal-residue-criterion] to $f|_U:U\to T$ at $z$. Restricting to an open subscheme leaves the local ring and the stalk map at a point unchanged; the restriction is locally of finite type by the affine-cover definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Step 3 gives the required maximal-ideal equality, and step 2 gives a residue extension of degree one, hence finite separable (every element has a linear minimal polynomial). We obtain an open $W\subseteq U$ containing $z$ with $f|_W$ unramified. By [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], $f|_W$ is smooth. By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] it is flat and locally of finite presentation; together with unramifiedness this is precisely etaleness by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Since $W$ is open in $U$ and $U$ is open in $Z$, it is the required open subscheme of $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, first proof paragraph; Tag 02GF (1) iff (6); Tag 02GK, lemma-etale-smooth-unramified

proof_origin.place: Tag 0CAV, lemma-isomorphism-approximation, first proof paragraph; the omitted Artinian lifting and maximal-ideal arguments expanded using Tag 02HX and Morphisms Tags 02GF and 02GK

from.place: The local criterion in the first paragraph of the proof of Tag 0CAV, used by Tag 0GDX in the nodal local-model branch of lem-trf-local-term-locality: the already constructed morphism is etale once its completed stalk map is an isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement unchanged after checking 0CAV. Expanded completed stalk isomorphism into compatible residue/first-order isomorphisms, Nakayama maximal-ideal equality, and explicit lifts for every small Artinian extension. Reused existing completion, local spectrum, Artinian and smoothness nodes. Created only the general scheme-point unramified criterion (02GF), with a Mathlib local-ring candidate distinguished from neighbourhood existence.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the historical nodal-model/completion-approximation branch recorded in blueprint.from: specifically the first paragraph of Tag 0CAV used below lem-trf-isomorphism-completion-approximation. Current main-20261015 lem-trf-local-term-locality uses the contracting-correspondence route and no longer spells out this historical auxiliary branch; no unit route or ancestor metadata is changed.

tool_uses.why: The standard small-Artinian lifting criterion proves smoothness of the already given morphism; this unit has no replacement for this general scheme tool.
Only the implication smooth implies flat and locally finitely presented is used to conclude etaleness; this is a general morphism criterion, not a replacement of a unit step.

lean.statement: theorem completedStalk_isomorphism_etale {Z T : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian T] (z : Z) (h : IsIso (CommRingCat.ofHom (completedStalkMap f z))) : ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ Etale (W.ι ≫ f) ∧ IsIso (f.residueFieldMap z)
